text:
sara_sales: Quick sync — FinServX is asking for an enterprise commit. They expect a steady-state of ~200 RPS for chat (mix of short prompts + multi-turn) and ~800 RPS embedding lookups during business hours, with bursts up to ~1.2k RPS. SLO: p99 chat < 300ms, embeddings p99 < 150ms. They want reserved capacity but also burst credits. Also incoming security questionnaire + KMS ask. Any red flags?

alex_deveng: Thanks — a couple quick clarifying q's: 1) average tokens per chat request? 2) embedding size model (512 vs 1536) and whether it's batched client-side?

sara_sales: Estimated avg chat: 60 tokens in, 80 tokens out. Embedding requests are small (single text -> 1536-d), clients will likely batch 8-16 on their side sometimes, but not always.

maria_se: For that mix we typically recommend: reserved pool sized for steady-state plus autoscale headroom. If embeddings are batched client-side, they amortize CPU/GPU overhead. Need KV cache assumptions for multi-turn?

sara_sales: Multi-turn ratio is ~30% of chat calls and we expect a warm KV cache on repeated users — but cold start expected for new users.

joe_infra: Operational note: suggest baseline reserved = capacity to serve 200 RPS chat + 400 RPS of embeddings (we'll let burst credits handle the rest). Rough mapping: with an A100-equivalent GPU, an optimized quantized chat model (seq len ~512) gives ~40-60 RPS for chat in low-latency config; embeddings throughput is much higher when batched. So reserved estimate -> 6-8 GPUs. Autoscale policy: min=6, target buffer=20% headroom, max=18 (reserve pool + burst autoscale).

maria_se: Also recommend model variants: quantized fp16 for reserve, int8 variant for burst (lower cost). Add fallback policy to route to cheaper region if latency still ok.

joe_infra: Preheat plan: KV warm will matter — we should run a 2-3 hour warmup with realistic traffic mix before handover. Example warmup snippet:```bash
# warmup simulator (simple)
for i in $(seq 1 1000); do
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood/engines/chat/generate \ 
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \ 
    -d '{"prompt":"short convo","max_tokens":80}' &
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood/engines/embed/embed -d '{"input":["sample text"]}' &
  sleep 0.05
done
wait
```

lena_pm: Security questionnaire items: they flagged KMS, audit logs retention, and VPC peering for Private deployments. @security-bot can you confirm what we can guarantee for a reserved Dedicated contract?

security-bot: KMS: supported (integrations with AWS KMS/GCP KMS). Audit logs: user/action logs retained per plan (can add extended retention as an add-on). VPC: Dedicated & Private support VPC peering and customer-controlled routing. We'll need the completed questionnaire to validate regulatory controls (PII fields). Link: https://redwood.internal/security/dedicated-reqs

deploy-bot: Scheduled canary deploy: quantized-int8 model lined up for canary at 2024-11-20T14:00Z (will run on 2 GPUs in staging).

sara_sales: Pricing q from FinServX: how much cheaper is a reserved GPU hour vs burst credits? They want concrete numbers to run internal TCO.

alex_deveng: Back-of-envelope: reserved commit (monthly) tends to be ~40-60% cheaper per GPU-hour than on-demand/burst credits depending on contract. Example: if on-demand-equivalent is $3.00/GPU-hour, committed rate might be $1.40-1.80/GPU-hour. For their expected steady workload (6-8 GPUs reserved) + burst usage (~spiky 6 GPUs for 2 hours/day) compute monthly delta. I can run a quick calc if they share expected burst hours.

maria_se: Recommendation to include in the proposal: reserved 8 GPUs (A100-eq) with autoscale to 16 for burst windows and a 20% CPU/GPU headroom buffer. Add preheat window (2-3 hours before go-live) and a 48-hour smoke test with synthetic traffic that matches the shape below. Include fallback model routing + KV cache warm script in runbook.

joe_infra: Synthetic traffic shape (for load testing):```json
{"duration_min":120,"steady_rps":{"chat":200,"embed":800},"burst_windows":[{"start_min":30,"duration_min":10,"peak_rps":{"chat":450,"embed":1200}}],"multiturn_pct":30}
```

sara_sales: Perfect. I'll add these numbers to the commercial proposal and ask FinServX to fill in the expected daily burst hours. One more ask: do we need any change to their client batching to hit embedding SLOs?

alex_deveng: If they batch embeddings >=8, p99 will be much better for embeddings. Recommend client-side batching or use our batching proxy. Also enable prefix/KV caching for repeat conversations to reduce chat cost and tail latency.

maria_se: I'll draft the runbook and questionnaire responses — will post a draft here by EOD.

sara_sales: Great — thanks team :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: Note: canary completed in staging with quantized-int8, latency delta +8% p99 vs fp16 but cost -40% in staging metrics.
